source.title: Sparsity as a Key: Unlocking New Insights from Latent Structures for Out-of-Distribution Detection
source.authors: Ah-Young Oh; Wonseok Shin; Songkuk Kim

record.tranche_reason: The study uses a Top-k SAE to produce sparse latent features for OOD detection, relying on the idea that sparse features can disentangle dense representations. It does not test the superposition or polysemanticity claims listed.
record.gate_note: The study reports class-level feature-set overlap and class activation profile geometry in a ViT. These are relevant to sparse latent representations, but they do not test whether features compete for limited capacity, whether SAE features are complete canonical units, or whether the original toy-model superposition account holds. OOD detection performance results and ID/OOD activation differences do not measure the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study trains a Top-k SAE on ViT-B/16 [CLS] embeddings and uses class-averaged latent activations to score out-of-distribution inputs. It cites superposition as motivation only. It reports no test of toy-model geometry, capacity competition, polysemanticity causes, or whether SAE features are complete, stable or canonical. Its geometry results (Jaccard overlap, UMAP clusters, CAP cosine similarity) are class-level statistics of the study's own SAE latent space, not measures of superposed feature directions. The subject is a vision model, not an LLM, so V4 does not apply.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that a Top-k SAE decomposes ViT [CLS] tokens into class-specific Class Activation Profiles, and that OOD inputs disrupt these profiles. Their divergence score (EPD) gives the best average FPR95 on ViT-B/16 (40.96%). They do not evaluate superposition claims. They note that individual latent neurons were not examined at the concept level.
record.recipe_differences: The original studies toy networks under controlled sparse-feature objectives; this study trains a Top-k SAE on ViT [CLS] embeddings and uses class activation profiles for OOD detection.
record.method_sensitivity: The study reports sensitivity sweeps for SAE latent dimension, sparsity level, and activation-head ratio for OOD detection, but does not show that these settings change any of the claim-version outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: In a ViT-B/16 Top-k SAE latent space, top-5% core-feature sets of ImageNet classes overlap near zero, except for semantically related classes.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE latents on vision-transformer [CLS] embeddings form largely class-specific feature sets.

fits_no_version.finding: Class centroids of sparse activations form well-separated clusters in a UMAP projection.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Class centroids in a ViT SAE latent space cluster by class and by semantic group.

fits_no_version.finding: Pairwise cosine similarity of class activation profiles peaks near zero; pairs with high similarity are semantically related.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Class mean SAE activation profiles in ViTs are mostly near-orthogonal, with similarity tracking semantic relatedness.

record.problems: The geometry evidence is presented qualitatively in figures without reported numerical summary statistics or uncertainty. The authors state that they did not conduct granular feature-level visualization to identify the concepts captured by individual latent neurons.
record.rows_left_out: OOD benchmark scores, baseline-method comparisons, and ID/OOD activation-profile differences were left out because they measure OOD detection performance or behavior, not the claim versions about superposition, capacity pressure, or feature units.

untested.parts: All parts: no toy model, no sparsity-dependent transition, no feature geometry in a bottleneck.
All parts: no analysis of neuron polysemanticity or capacity allocation.
All parts: no LLMs studied; no measure of how features spread across ViT neurons.
Completeness, stability across seeds or sizes, and canonicity of SAE features. The latent dimension and k sweeps report only OOD scores.

record.verdict_notes: The paper cites Toy Models of Superposition only as motivation, saying concepts are 'superposed within dense activations'. This is an OOD-detection methods paper. The latent dimension (L) and sparsity level (k) sweeps report only OOD performance, plus an unquantified remark about reconstruction quality. All geometry evidence is figure-only with no numbers.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-model superposition, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry of overlapping feature directions.
Whether polysemanticity results from capacity competition or importance-dependent sharing.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise without capacity pressure.
The version concerns LLMs; this study analyzes vision models and does not test feature spread across LLM neurons.
The study analyzes class-level averages of SAE activations, not whether individual SAE features are complete, stable, canonical units.
Whether represented features are one-dimensional directions or multidimensional.

rows.subject: ViT-B/16 with Top-k SAE
rows.operation_detail: Compared top-5% core latent-feature sets for each of 1,000 ImageNet classes using pairwise Jaccard similarity.

conditions.value: top 5% of latent neurons ranked by mean class activation

rows.measure: Pairwise Jaccard similarity of class core-feature sets
rows.value: Near-zero off-diagonal similarity; occasional weak overlap between semantically related categories.
rows.note: The text describes minimal cross-class overlap. This is class-level feature-set disjointness, not a test of feature superposition or capacity competition.
rows.check: Class-level core-feature-set overlap within the SAE latent space. It does not measure superposition, capacity competition or feature canonicity. The row's state 'observed' refers to the study's own hypothesis, not to any claim version.

rows.subject: ViT-B/16 with Top-k SAE
rows.operation_detail: Visualized class-centroid mean sparse activation vectors using UMAP.
rows.measure: Separation of class mean sparse activation vectors in UMAP projection
rows.value: The 1,000 classes form tight, well-separated clusters in the projection.
rows.note: The visualization concerns class centroids in a projected latent space, not individual feature directions.
rows.check: A UMAP figure of class centroids in SAE space, qualitative only. The value describes separation of class means, not feature directions.

rows.subject: ViT-B/16 with Top-k SAE
rows.operation_detail: Measured pairwise cosine similarity between the mean activation profiles (CAPs) of 1,000 ImageNet classes.
rows.measure: Pairwise cosine similarity of class activation profiles
rows.value: The distribution peaks near zero; the text says most class pairs occupy nearly orthogonal subspaces, with higher similarity for semantically related pairs.
rows.note: The measurement concerns class-level mean activation profiles, not directions that encode individual features.
rows.check: Near-orthogonality is between class mean activation profiles in a 7680-dimensional sparse space, not between feature directions in a lower-dimensional space. It is unrelated to V1 geometry.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
